bounded_slice.candidate: Candidate-amplification replay for DSSE keyid routing with a 16-key independently configured candidate set and deterministic maximum-candidate fail-closed policy.
bounded_slice.tested_scope: Replayed the exact persisted p1-sa-583 DSSE payload/signature. Rebuilt DSSE PAE and verified the existing signature against 16 configured Ed25519 public-key candidates whose membership/order was independent of envelope keyid. Candidates 1-15 are deterministic synthetic negative controls derived from explicitly nonsecret fixed seeds byte(i)*32 for i=1..15; candidate 16 is the prior configured K1. Missing or ambiguous routing selects all 16. Tested caps 4, 8, and 16.

primary_spec_inherited.observation: KEYID is optional and unauthenticated, excluded from PAE/signature input, MUST NOT be used for security decisions, and may only narrow candidate-key selection.

inputs.candidate_generation: candidate[1..15] = Ed25519 public keys derived from synthetic nonsecret private-byte test vectors byte(i)*32 for i=1..15; candidate[16]=K1; candidate order fixed before routing metadata is applied.

bounded_slice.observation: With K1 placed last, ambiguous/absent routing caused 16 actual Ed25519 verification attempts and only K1 verified; none of 15 synthetic negative candidates verified. Compared with the prior two-key enumeration this is an 8x worst-case verification-attempt increase. A deterministic cap below the candidate-set size bounded verification work to zero by rejecting before cryptographic verification, while cap=16 allowed the valid signature to be found at attempt 16.
bounded_slice.inference: For this exact fixture, unauthenticated routing ambiguity can linearly amplify verification work when a verifier enumerates an independently configured candidate set. A deterministic maximum-candidate policy can fail closed and bound that work without creating false acceptance, but it creates a liveness/availability tradeoff because a genuinely valid configured key can be rejected when the candidate set exceeds the cap. Routing metadata still provides no trust or authorization.
bounded_slice.uncertainty: Not tested: wall-clock CPU scaling across implementations/hardware, adversarially chosen expensive key types, normalization/prefix-collision routing, multi-signature thresholds, authorization/revocation/freshness, trust-root distribution, package-plus-trust-material replacement, PKI, or cross-implementation interoperability. This 16-key Ed25519 fixture establishes verification-attempt growth only, not a general DoS bound.
